summary: Michigan City Breakwater Light, Indiana: an 1904 post light on the detached breakwater, replaced after a 1909 storm by a 23-foot concrete tower in 1911.

lens.note: Beacon lens upgraded in the 1970s (NRHP p. 6).

structures.note: 23 ft (7 m) including the tank house; the pyramidal tower is 16 ft. Painted red 1911-1969, white 1969-1999, white with a red band since 1999.

staffing.note: Acetylene buoy lantern ran automatically except for replacing its tanks (NRHP p. 6).

access.note: Reached only by boat; not open to public visitation (NRHP p. 4). Keep-off sign on the tank house (NRHP p. 5).

Red horizontal band added to the white tower
Nomination cover bears a 9 June 2017 date stamp (NRHP 100001344)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination says the 1911 AGA lantern was originally flashing (p. 6) and also that it signaled a fixed red light (p. 18). LighthouseFriends describes the 1904 post light as fixed red. The record's present Fl R 4s is the current red flash (p. 5). The sources do not settle when the flash began; the story says so.

The record dates the light to 1911 (its built year). The nomination and LighthouseFriends show a fixed red post light from 1904 (established 20 October 1904), replaced after the 1909 storm by the 1911 tower. The facts block uses 1904 for first light.
The nomination says visible for six miles in clear weather, without naming statute or nautical miles. The record's 5.2 nm equals 6 statute miles. The facts block keeps the record's value.

notes_for_editor: No keeper roster for the breakwater light. The USLHS keeper lists are for the station: Michigan City (Old) (Colfax 1861-1904) and East Pierhead (Armstrong 1904-1918). The link from the station to the breakwater light rests on LighthouseFriends' count of three lights and fog signal from 1904 (the east pierhead, the breakwater and the west pierhead). No source names a keeper for the breakwater light, and the story says so. Not used: a 1916 Lighthouse Service Bulletin account of a 1915 rescue of two men 'caught on the end of the breakwater near the light station' names the keeper of the East Pierhead station (Thomas J. Armstrong); it is not this light and is not counted. The Commissioner of Lighthouses report for fiscal 1915 lists 'Michigan City Breakwater, Mich.' among the district's lights (scan p. 42, printed p. 37); the story does not use it. The USLHS place record 'Michigan City west Breakwater' is a minor aid recorded as Existing: No, and it is listed as a source page for this light. The nomination describes a 1911 concrete tower at the northeast end of the detached breakwater, so that link needs checking; no USLHS place record for this tower was found. The 1909 storm: LighthouseFriends dates the loss to February 1909; the Lake County Times item of 28 July 1909 (second-hand, quoting the Michigan City Dispatch) reports the detached breakwater damaged by a storm the previous winter. The Dispatch was not checked directly. The same Hammond paper's other 1909-1912 hits were not relevant. The nomination's OCR reads 'the USLHS 1th Lighthouse District'; that number was not used.
